subject: POC onboarding + capacity confirmation — Acme Logistics trial
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC onboarding + capacity confirmation — Acme Logistics trial

Hi Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a mutual action plan before the kickoff:  

Summary of call:
- Goal: Validate inference latency and cost for routing/ETL use case (peak event-based routing across 3 regions).
- Success criteria (tentative): p95 gen latency <= 180ms for 512-token requests, end-to-end throughput 400 reqs/min sustained, token cost <= $0.006/token equivalent in our hosted metrics.
- Data handling: no PHI; logs retained for 30 days; model inputs sampled for quality checks only.

Immediate asks / next actions:
1) Redwood: propose capacity plan for a 2-week POC (reserved + burst), provide runbook & SLA draft — Dev is on this and will share an initial capacity spreadsheet and runbook.
2) Acme: confirm target workload distribution (avg vs peak), procurement timeline for PO/contract, and point of contact for environment/network access.
3) Agree kickoff week: we suggested Apr 26 — you said hopeful this week works but will confirm with procurement.

Attachments we'll send: capacity estimate spreadsheet, POC runbook, and a short SLA draft for mutual review.

If the success criteria above look off, tell me which metric you want adjusted and we'll update. Planning to loop in engineering on Thursday for the capacity plan deliverable.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0104

From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-logistics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acme-logistics.com>, procurement-acme@acme-logistics.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onboarding + capacity confirmation — Acme Logistics trial

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:  

- Success criteria: p95 latency target of 180ms is fine, but can we also add a secondary metric around cold-starts? If a model variant is loaded fresh, we'd like cold-starts < 800ms for first token.
- Workload distribution: typical steady-state ~120 reqs/min, predictable bursts up to 520 reqs/min during routing spikes (10–15 minute windows), roughly 60% of traffic from US-east, 30% EU, 10% APAC.
- Data access: we will provide a test dataset and a staging VPC peering (no private keys). Daniel (cc'd) is our platform lead and will own environment setup. Procurement loop: procurement-acme will need an initial statement of work and capacity estimate for the PO.

We can confirm kickoff the week of Apr 26 — procurement asked for the capacity numbers and an estimate of reserved vs burst GPUs by Friday Apr 16. Can you get that to us?

Best,
Priya
Head of Product, Acme Logistics
priya@acme-logistics.com

Subject: Re: POC onboarding + capacity confirmation — Acme Logistics trial

Hi Priya / Jonas — attaching the capacity worksheet and a concise runbook. High level proposal below followed by assumptions.

Proposal (2-week POC):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A10G-equivalent VMs (quantized model), dedicated to Acme in US-east for steady-state 120 reqs/min. This covers p95 target and gives headroom for autoscaling control.
- Autoscaling: target policy scales in steps: +1 instance at 220 reqs/min, +2 instances at 360 reqs/min, +3 instances at 480 reqs/min. Scale cooldown 90s to avoid flapping.
- Burst/spot capacity: allow additional preemptible instances in same region to reach up to 8 instances total (estimated capacity ~640 reqs/min) for short bursts. Preemptible pooling triggers at sustained >480 reqs/min for >60s.
- Cold-start mitigation: keep a lightweight warm pool of 1 instance per region (US-east, EU-west) with prompt-based keepalive; expected cold-starts <600ms based on similar evals.
- Networking: use VPC peering; test dataset will be pulled from your staging S3 bucket via IAM role; no secrets stored on instances.

Estimated cost (2 weeks): reserved baseline + autoscale + expected burst = see attached spreadsheet. Rough estimate: $18k–$26k depending on spot availability.

Attachments: acme_poc_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with hourly projection), redwood_poc_runbook_v1.md (playbook: deploy, monitor, rollback), redwood_trial_sla_draft.pdf (SLA + success criteria annex).

Assumptions / questions for Acme:
1) Confirm regional preference for the EU warm pool (we suggested EU-west);
2) Can procurement sign an abbreviated SOW for trial spend authorization or do you need a full PO?
3) Do you want us to front any credit for spot/overage while procurement completes the PO? We can consider a limited credit for first week.

If that looks good I can lock the autoscale thresholds and run through a quick ops dry-run with your platform team next Tuesday.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: POC onboarding + capacity confirmation — Acme Logistics trial

Priya / team — thanks Dev, that plan looks aligned with what we discussed. Two quick operational notes and proposed mutual action plan:  

Operational clarifications:
- We will reserve 2 baseline instances for the POC in US-east for the full 2 weeks. Autoscale will be reactive per Dev's thresholds; spot pool is optional and can be gated by Acme procurement.
- SOW: we'll provide a one-page trial SOW (scope + cost ceiling) you can attach to the PO. If procurement prefers a PO upfront we can accept a small deposit and hold capacity.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Apr 16 (EOD): Redwood sends final capacity spreadsheet and 1-page trial SOW (Dev to finalize).
- Apr 19: Acme confirms PO path / deposit or approves trial SOW.
- Apr 22: Ops dry-run with Acme platform (30–45 min) to validate VPC peering and sample dataset access. Dev to lead.
- Apr 26: POC kickoff (run for 2 weeks).

Please reply with any changes to dates and we'll adapt. If procurement needs a revised cost ceiling to approve faster, tell us the number and we'll trim spot/overage exposure.

I'll attach the 1-page SOW when Dev confirms the final numbers — aiming for EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-logistics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Jonas / Dev — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement confirmed they can approve a $20k ceiling for the trial as an initial PO. That should be sufficient if the spot pool is capped and Redwood covers the first-week overage credit. Can you update the SOW to reflect a $20k not-to-exceed and a credit line for week 1?

We also confirm Apr 22 for the ops dry-run — Daniel will coordinate with Dev on exact time. If all goes well we'll lock Apr 26 kickoff.

Thanks — Priya
